text: You just filled your gas car with diesel. Here's what you do.
First, don't turn the key. Even switching it on runs the fuel pump and pushes diesel deeper.
Here's why: your engine lights its fuel with a spark.
But diesel is thick and oily, and a spark can't light it.
Start it anyway, and you drive a few miles on leftover gas, then it knocks, shakes, and dies.
So call a tow truck, and have a shop drain the tank.
Wondering how it even fit? Diesel nozzles are made too wide for most gas tanks.
Caught at the pump, a tow and a drain run a few hundred bucks.
Drive it till it dies, and new parts can top three thousand dollars.
And that's what to do when you put diesel in a gas car.
